exposure: timing of hospital admission in labour (active phase (>=5 cm) vs. second stage)
outcome: intrapartum interventions (artificial rupture of membranes, oxytocin augmentation)
mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, caesarean section)
cohort: 172 women at >=37 weeks gestation admitted in spontaneous labour at a tertiary care hospital in southern India.
finding: Admission after confirmed onset of active labour (>=5 cm) is associated with reduced intrapartum interventions and lower operative delivery rates.
mod_finding: Admission in active labour was associated with lower operative delivery rates, with specific causes for caesarean section differing by admission timing (cephalopelvic disproportion in active labour vs. deep transverse arrest in second stage).
